theThreeGates.independentAdjudication: Evidence from adjudicators who are not the author and never saw the key. Strong evidence, not proof.
theThreeGates.humanReview: A person taking responsibility. Nothing substitutes for it and no pack ships without it.

retiredPacks.retiredBecause: SUPERSEDED REASON, kept for the record: it was retired on 4 September 2026 for failing the original §5.10, which required a pack to contribute a materially non-generic relationship. That rule was withdrawn on 5 September 2026 because the official material fails it — Exercise 3 is the optimal order quantity model, a textbook formula, with a stated-assumption question, comparative statics, a pure plug-in on source-supplied values and a chart-reading question. This pack matched that exercise question for question, which is why it was retired.

Superseded by the production candidate set of 8-9 September 2026, and retired on promotion rather than deleted. No key in this pack is wrong: two independent rounds agreed with every one of them, and it carries no ambiguity, outside-knowledge or §5.10 finding. It is retired because of how it was built. It predates the independent-source architecture, and under the same adjudicator that cleared the candidate set every one of the pilot’s sixteen questions carried a narrowing sibling coupling, against seven of nineteen in the set replacing it. Keeping both active would ship two authoring standards at once. Its questions, provenance and adjudication history are kept in full as the record of how the architecture was arrived at; the ids are reserved and never reused.

Fails spec §5.9 at pack level. The independent round of 8 September 2026 — Claude Opus 5 on both halves, neither shown the answer key — rated six of the pack’s seven questions DECISIVELY coupled, and demonstrated the mechanism: the option lists reconstruct Table 1 in full without the table being seen. q7’s options factor exactly into SPLIT(4096) = 340 and SCAN(4096) = 16,414; q2’s options are spaced by exactly 25 and q3 asserts a constant rise per doubling, giving SPLIT(n) = 40 + 25 log2 n; q5’s first option is SCAN(256), giving SCAN(n) = 4n + 30; q1’s 128 and 32,768 stand in the ratio of one table step squared, giving PAIR(n) = n^2 / 2. Every row of the table follows, and with it six of the seven answers. No key is wrong — both rounds agreed with all seven — and there is no ambiguity, outside-knowledge or §5.10 finding against it. The fault is the arithmetic relationship between the option lists, which is a pack-level design fault: each item is individually sound. Retiring the six coupled questions would leave one, so this is retirement under its proper name. A replacement should carry at most two numeric items on one table, or use a source whose questions do not all reduce to arithmetic on the same few constants. Kept in full as the evidence; counts for nothing.

packs.title: A cache and its replacement policy

contributesUnderSection510.whatItContributes: p1 and p2 supply the hit/miss definitions, the full-cache eviction requirement and the eviction rule including the decisive clause that a hit re-counts as an asking - without that clause Q1's answer flips from Q to P, so the source is genuinely load-bearing there. t1 supplies the four measured hit rates Q3 reads off, and p3 supplies the caveat Q4 restates that hit rates describe a cache-plus-traffic pairing rather than ranking the caches.

not signed off by a person

decisions.question: Spec §5.10 requires the source to contribute something the question uses, and the question to apply it rather than repeat it. The adjudicator found 0 question(s) the source contributes nothing to and 2 that ask only for recall. Are those judgements right?

evidence.note: The rule was corrected on 5 September 2026: a standard relationship applied to source-supplied values passes, because that is what official Exercise 3 does. Only a question whose answer is unchanged with the source removed entirely fails.

decisions.question: 1 question(s) can be narrowed — not settled — using a sibling: gam-cs-cp-001-q4. Is the cost to each item acceptable, or must they be rebuilt? Spec §5.9 leaves this to a person because severity is a judgement.

evidence.detail: DOCTRINAL COUPLING succeeds in the stem-presupposition direction, and it is the one real coupling in this pack. q3's stem asks the reader to identify which cache 'met the smallest share of its requests without going to the slow store' — an ordinary comparative read across the table's rows, which the pack evidently treats as a legitimate and answerable question. That presupposition directly undercuts two of this item's four options. Option c claims the figures 'cannot be compared because the caches hold different numbers of records'; if that were the text's position, q3 would be asking the reader to perform a comparison the same source declares impossible. Option d claims a single day's hit rate is 'too short a period to be used at all'; that likewise would void the read q3 requires. Both are therefore improbable as the intended answer, narrowing this item from four options to a and b before any domain reasoning is applied. From there a falls to ordinary knowledge, leaving b. The narrowing is real but not decisive on its own, and it is redundant here because I reach b with high confidence from domain knowledge alone — so it inflates a solver's odds on this item without being the reason a competent solver gets it right. The remaining patterns fail: NUMERIC RECONSTRUCTION has no numbers to work with; SCALE DISCLOSURE is inapplicable, since q3's options are row labels with no magnitudes and cannot calibrate anything here; SHARED PARAMETER holds between this item and q3 (both read the same four-design table) but is inherent to a pack built on one source rather than a leak; CONVENTION AS CONSTANT fails, since no eviction policy figures in this item; ANSWER-AS-DISTRACTOR fails, since no sibling's correct answer appears among these options. q1 contributes nothing in either direction — I checked whether its 'a cache holds three records' could inform option c's claim about differing record counts and it cannot, as q1's cache is a separate hypothetical.

evidence.detail: DOCTRINAL COUPLING. q3's correct answer is that a rate is unchanged when only volume changes — the pack's posture that rates are properties of the process, independent of scale. Carrying that posture across kills q2's option d ('adjusted in proportion to the change in output'), which is the same scaling error q3's option b commits. One distractor falls without the source; the remaining choice among a, b and c still needs the text.

The converse of the coupling on q2: q2 asks what must happen when the process itself changes, and its option set treats re-measurement as the live issue, which signals that the pack holds rates constant under volume and revisable only under process change. That reinforces a and undercuts b and c here. The item is independently determinable, so this is reinforcement rather than a decision.

evidence.detail: DOCTRINAL COUPLING. Every option q4 offers as the condition for a figure to count as an agreement rate is procedural — independence, equal double-coding, an unrevised frame, exclusions — which tells a candidate the statistic is a coder-level, procedural one. That argues against q3's a and d, which are validity claims, without any recourse to the source. The item is independently answerable, so the coupling reinforces rather than decides.

Two coupled routes. From q3: if the rate measures whether two coders read the frame the same way, independence is the condition that makes that reading possible, so q3's answer supports a. From q2: q2's answer has contested answers marked and still coded, which undercuts d ('contested answers were excluded before the rate was worked out'). Both are reasons available from siblings rather than from the source, and together they leave a against two weak procedural rivals.
